lens: Product and UX lead: flow, hierarchy and patterns against best-in-class (Apple HIG and Apple's own apps, Day One, Apple Journal, Headspace, Calm, Tinybeans, Qeepsake, Huckleberry, Things, Bear, Overcast)
coverage: Read on origin/develop: CLAUDE.md, packages/content/VOICE.md and BRAND.md, docs/brand/BRAND_SYSTEM.md, docs/design/DESIGN_LANGUAGE.md, BENCHMARK.md, MOTION.md, CREATIVE.md, COMPONENT_LIBRARY.md, COMPONENTS.md, packages/design-tokens/src/tokens.ts, every copy source in packages/content/src (strings.en.ts in full, stories, pages, prompts, permissions, book), the screen code for the age gate, onboarding, Tonight and line-art, and the legal sources for the age question (docs/legal/ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENTS.md LEGAL-REQ-002, docs/prd/PRD.md K-07 and PRD-REQ-019, docs/DECISIONS.md D-006 and D-026, compliance-register CR-004/CR-006 and open counsel question Q6). Read on origin/main apps/web: Landing.tsx, Aurora.tsx and its CSS, Landing.module.css, PinScene, ProofLetter, Evening, StoryRail, globals.css, content/site.ts, plus three earlier phone captures of the live site (hero, Evening, proof letter). Journey record from origin/chore/journey-refresh in a worktree: INDEX.md and all 147 steps/*.json read in full; screenshots looked at for every distinct screen, light and dark, including J00-open, J01-01/02/03/04/05/07/09/10/12/14/15/16-full/17/18, J02-02/04, J03-05/07/08/21/31/32, J04-01/04, J05-01/02/03/04, J06-01-full/03-full/04/06/08/09/13/14, J07-01/02/03/08, J08-02/03/06, J09-01/03/03-full/04/05, J10-01/03/05/06/08/10/11/12/14, J11-01/03/04/07, J12-01/02, J13-01/02-full, J14-01, J15-01/02, J16-01-full/02/03/05-full/06-full, J17-01-full/03-full, J18-02/03/04/05/06, J19-01/02, J20-01/02. Also inspected the unmerged side branches feat/app-lamp-wash (LampWash component with a light-mode contrast test) and feat/mobile-calm-brand (atmosphere tokens, lamp.tsx, quote-pair.tsx) so the gradient proposals name real primitives. Two findings about the brief itself: (1) A-REQ-030 in docs/prd/A-entry-and-auth.md is "Offline entry", not the age gate; the journey index mislabels it. The age question's real sources are LEGAL-REQ-002, PRD-REQ-019, K-07, D-006 and D-026. (2) BRAND_SYSTEM.md section 4 says "Never: a gradient anywhere except the app icon tile", which conflicts with the founder's ask for the website's lamp light in the app; the proposals below need that one brand line amended (the side branches already drafted the atmosphere token and its 4.5:1 contrast test). Benchmark verification: Apple HIG pages were read today from Apple's documentation JSON for onboarding, privacy, pickers, entering data, settings, launching, feedback, managing accounts, managing notifications, writing, loading and modality (quoted where cited). The HIG in-app purchase page returned 404 from that endpoint, so it is cited from memory. dayoneapp.com and apple.com were unreachable from this sandbox, so Day One, Apple Journal, Headspace, Calm, Tinybeans, Qeepsake, Huckleberry, Things, Bear and Overcast are cited from memory and marked unverified, except where docs/design/BENCHMARK.md records its own primary-source read (S5 Journal newsroom, S6 Day One features, S7 Headspace, S8 Things, S9 Apple Books, M10 Calm), marked "verified in repo BENCHMARK.md". Scope respected: sign-in, sync, co-parent and backup surfaces (Family tab, invite sheet, "Write this book together" row) are marked held and not redesigned. All 147 step ids are grouped into the 49 screens below.
principles: Arrival before admin. The first thing anyone sees is the brand and one line; a required question (the age gate) is the first tap, never the first screen, and no setup is asked for that the first letter does not need. Benchmark: Apple HIG Onboarding, "Postpone nonessential setup flows or customization steps" and "Prefer letting people experience your app or game before prompting them" (verified today from Apple's documentation JSON); HIG Managing accounts, "Delay sign-in for as long as possible" (verified today).

One job per screen, one primary. Every screen has a single next step in the thumb zone; quiet alternatives sit beneath it; nothing explains a second feature on the way. Benchmark: Apple HIG Modality, "Aim to keep modal tasks simple, short, and streamlined" (verified today); Things 3 one-list-one-action framing (verified in repo BENCHMARK.md S8).

Say the thing, never why. No "we ask", "we sort", "this is how"; no preamble before a question; a promise is said once where someone might wonder and nowhere else. Benchmark: Apple HIG Writing, "Check each word to be sure it needs to be there" and "Avoid using we altogether" (verified today); VOICE.md "Do not repeat the promise on screens where nobody is wondering".

Show, do not tell. The small-fixes promise is taught by a letter you can tap, the empty book by one drawing and one line, the download by a size and a button, not by paragraphs. Benchmark: Apple HIG Onboarding, "Teach through interactivity" (verified today); the website's ProofLetter scene (read on origin/main); Headspace illustration-led first run (verified in repo BENCHMARK.md S7).

Light is the atmosphere, paper is the page. The website's lamp wash (amber by evening, dusk late) arrives once behind moments: welcome, the open book, Tonight at night, the end of Read together, the Plus sheet. It never sits behind the letter text, the Book list, a settings list or the brand mark, and it is static under Reduce Motion. Benchmark: apps/web Aurora.tsx on origin/main (read); Calm's single full-bleed scene behind its welcome (memory, unverified); DESIGN_LANGUAGE 2 contrast floors kept by the LampWash contrast test on feat/app-lamp-wash.

Receipts, not interruptions. A save commits first and the motion is the receipt; reversible loss gets an undo toast, not a confirm page; only unexpected, irreversible loss gets a sheet. Benchmark: Apple HIG Feedback, "reserve this type of confirmation for activities that are sufficiently important" and "Warn people when they initiate a task that can cause data loss that's unexpected and irreversible" (verified today); Apple Mail Undo Send and Photos Recently Deleted (memory, unverified).

Settings feel like Settings. Grouped inset lists, sentence-case subtitles, infrequent options only, one switch per decision, long content pushed to its own page, never an accordion inside the list. Benchmark: Apple HIG Settings, "Minimize the number of settings you offer" and "Put general, infrequently changed settings in your custom settings area" (verified today); iOS Settings grouped lists (observed).

Honest gates, equal doors. The Plus gate says what stays free, lets Apple's sheet show the price, and always offers a calm way out; Speak and Type stay identical twins; no streaks, counts of gaps or urgency anywhere. Benchmark: Apple HIG In-App Purchase, present purchases at a natural moment and use the system sheet (memory, unverified; the JSON endpoint 404ed); Overcast Premium's plain one-screen upgrade (memory, unverified); App Store Review Guideline 3.1.2 on clear subscription terms (memory).

screens.problem: It is the first thing anyone sees: a bare form on blank paper with a quiz-style Yes/No, a greyed Continue, and the line "We ask everyone the same question.", which explains the asking instead of asking. No calm consumer app opens on a compliance question; the ones that gate (social, alcohol) ask a birthday, and the calm ones (Headspace, Calm, Day One, Tinybeans, Huckleberry; memory, unverified) ask nothing and rely on the App Store rating. The legal team has decided a neutral question is required here, so the job is to make it the smallest, most dignified moment possible, not the front door.
screens.proposal: Move the question off the first screen and into the first tap. The welcome screen (brand, one line, "Begin the book") is the first thing anyone sees. Tapping "Begin the book" opens a short non-dismissible sheet (ui/sheet with dismissible={false}, fitToContents, grabber hidden): title in title1 serif "Are you 18 or older?"; beneath it two equal pill rows, nothing preselected, "Yes" and "No" at the same size, weight and colour; one full-width "Continue" that enables on a choice (the confirming tap is kept on purpose: a No closes the app for 24 hours, so a mis-tap must not be one gesture). No sentence under the title. No lock icon, no illustration, no lamp wash: this sheet stays quiet. The whole thing is two taps and under three seconds. Implementation: keep useAgeGate() at the root so no route past the static welcome page is reachable until it passes; deep links land on welcome. Where the Declared Age Range API is available (Texas), call it in memory as today; an adult result does not skip the question unless counsel answers Q6 that way.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Onboarding: "Postpone nonessential setup flows" and "Avoid displaying licensing details within your onboarding flow... If you must include these items... integrate them in a balanced way that doesn't disrupt the experience" (verified today). HIG Privacy pre-alert screens: "Include only one button... Use a term like Continue" (verified today). Apple's own App Store age confirmation for 17+ apps is a two-option alert, not a page (memory, unverified). Birth-year pickers (Instagram, TikTok; memory, unverified) collect more than needed and HIG Privacy says "Request access only to data that you actually need" (verified today).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: Requirement is LEGAL-REQ-002 (docs/legal/ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENTS.md), PRD-REQ-019, PRD K-07, D-006, D-026; the journey index's A-REQ-030 is a mislabel (that id is Offline entry). What must hold: the question appears before any child detail, recording or invite, with nothing preselected and no hint that one answer is right; only a boolean is stored after Yes and only a timestamp after No; no retry for 24 hours; store signals used in memory only. The proposal satisfies LEGAL-REQ-002's first criterion as written ("When the user takes any first action (start a book...), Then the age question appears first"): the welcome page holds no data and is not an action. D-026's "root-level boot gate" stays as implementation. Removing the explanatory line and the Continue-after-choice shape change nothing legal. Dropping a birth-year picker respects "never store a birth date or age range". Counsel's open question Q6 (compliance-register s.6) still decides whether a positive Declared Age Range may replace the question; until then the question stays.

screens.problem: "Thank you for telling us." is a customer-service nicety, and "Nothing you entered has been kept." invents a worry: nothing was entered. Three lines where one is true. After 24 hours "I answered by mistake" asks the person to confess.
screens.proposal: One line in title1 serif, centred on paper, no icon: "For now, {app} is for adults 18 and over." Nothing else on the screen. After 24 hours a single quiet button beneath it: "Answer again". Keep the VoiceOver announcement of the title on arrival.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Writing: "Check each word to be sure it needs to be there"; "Interjections... can sound insincere" (verified today). Apple's own unavailable-content screens state the fact in one line (App Store "not available in your country or region"; memory, unverified).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: LEGAL-REQ-002 requires the stop screen to explain the app is currently for adults 18 and over, store only the gate state, and stay closed 24 hours (D-026 removed the instant retry). The proposed line keeps "for now" and "adults 18 and over". No fear or guilt language; {app} comes from packages/brand.

screens.problem: Good bones, but it is flat paper with a drawing, and it retypes the product name in Literata as a hero title, which BRAND_SYSTEM forbids ("Never retype the name in a font to stand in for the lockup"). It also carries three lines of description, the descriptor the person already read on the App Store, and no atmosphere at all, when the website opens on lamp light and a single literary line.
screens.proposal: Make it the arrival. Background: LampWash (feat/app-lamp-wash) anchored top, amber, arriving over 1200 ms (tokens.motion.lamp.arriveMs from feat/mobile-calm-brand), static under Reduce Motion; light mode stays a whisper, dark mode carries the website's amber. Top: the small-cut lockup from the registry (context app.header, 24 pt), the only logo on the screen. Middle: the open-envelope drawing drawn on once (DrawOnPath, 1.2 s), then the hero line in Literata 44: "Letters for someone small." (the line DESIGN_LANGUAGE 12 and CREATIVE 6 already set), with one muted line under it: "The baby memory book you fill by talking." Then the one quiet line D-082 asks for: "Your first two letters are free." Delete the body sentence "A few words at a time, in your own voice. Kept for your child to read and hear for years." Bottom: "Begin the book", full width, 56 pt. Motion: dateline-style stagger (280 ms, 30 ms) on the lines only; the button never animates in. Deserves the illustration and the light; no photograph.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Launching: "Downplay the launch experience"; HIG Onboarding: splash "just long enough for people to absorb the information at a glance" (verified today). Calm's welcome: one full-bleed scene, one serif line, one button (memory, unverified). Headspace: illustration-led, one line per screen (verified in repo BENCHMARK.md S7). The website hero on origin/main: name in serif on the lamp aurora, one lead line (read).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: BRAND_SYSTEM 2 (wordmark is artwork, one logo per screen) is satisfied by using the registry lockup. BRAND_SYSTEM 4 "gradient anywhere except the app icon tile" needs one amendment to allow the atmosphere wash behind content, never behind the mark; the side branches already carry the contrast test. D-082 free line kept. "I was invited" stays hidden (held: co-parent scope).

screens.problem: A text explainer: two paragraphs, two cards, a footnote and a cute button ("That sounds right") before the person has done anything. It tells the Word for word promise instead of showing it, and "This is Word for word." names a feature nobody has met yet.
screens.proposal: Show the proof. Title: "Exactly as you said it." Under it, one line: "We never rewrite your words." Then the sample letter as the app renders a Review: the fictional Asha spoon letter with its two small fixes already marked ("um," taken out, the repeated "you" struck through), the chip "2 small fixes", and the marks tappable: tapping one shows "You said" and "Put it back", so the person learns the gesture here. Beneath the letter, two footnote lines with icons and no card chrome: microphone icon, "The recording stays on this phone."; seal icon, the counsel-reviewed disclosure sentence from settings.help.mistakes verbatim: "Your words are kept as you said them. We can mishear, so read each letter and fix anything we got wrong." Drop "Private by default. You choose what goes in the book." (it is said again on Listening). Button: "Continue". Keep the step: the mishear disclosure must be met before the first save, and this is where it earns its place.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Onboarding: "Teach through interactivity... provide an interactive onboarding experience where people can safely test an action" (verified today). The website's ProofLetter scene draws each fix as you scroll (read on origin/main). Day One shows a sample entry rather than describing one (memory, unverified).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: Constitution: the sample is fixed by the allowed EditType kinds (filler, repeat) and adds no meaning; the sample letter must be fictional (Asha) and must pass verifyEdits like the web sample does in test/sample-letter.test.ts. in-app-disclosures.md section 2 places the mishear note here and on the first Review; keep the sentence verbatim. VOICE: "Word for word" is named only where the feature is named (the promise, Settings, store, website), so naming it in a caption on the sample is not allowed; the title carries the promise instead.

screens.screen: Who is this book for (name, birthday or due date, twins)
screens.problem: The right questions, but the screen explains itself three times: "You can add a nickname later." (a feature v1.0 does not have), "We sort letters by Asha's month of age." (why we ask), and a standing instruction above the disabled button ("Choose Asha's birthday to continue.") that reads as an error before anyone has erred. The web build shows mm/dd/yyyy; on iPhone the compact date picker is right.
screens.proposal: Keep the heading "Who is this book for?" and the field label "Their name" with the placeholder. Delete the nickname helper. Keep the segmented "Birthday | Not here yet" and the compact date picker beside the label, with the quiet "Born today" link. Replace "We sort letters by Asha's month of age." with nothing; replace the due-date helper with "Letters written before the birthday go in Before You." Keep Continue disabled until the data is there, and show the why-line only after a tap on the disabled button (wrap it in a Pressable that reveals the line in a polite live region and focuses the empty field); the line itself stays as written ("Choose Asha's birthday to continue."). Twins: unchanged. No illustration here; this screen stays quiet.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Entering data: "make the button available only after people enter the data you require" and "Dynamically validate field values" (verified today). HIG Pickers: compact date picker, "Avoid switching views to show a picker" (verified today). Huckleberry and Tinybeans first run ask only name and birth date with an expecting option (memory, unverified).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: Birthday is L4 data (PRD 7.10) and stays on the phone. No gendered words; the child is named by the parent. Due date range (305 days) and no-future-birthday rules unchanged.

screens.screen: What does Asha call you (signature and spoken language)
screens.problem: The best-designed step: chips fill the field and the italic "From Mama" preview sells it. But "This is how your letters will be signed." explains what the preview already shows, and the language row's footer "Your words stay in the language you speak. We never translate them." is a promise nobody asked about here.
screens.proposal: Delete the subtitle. Keep the field, the chips under "A few ideas", the live italic preview "From Mama" (scale 1.3), and the warm fallback "Not talking yet? Pick the name you hope to hear." Keep the "Spoken language" row with its native-name value and remove its footer. Button stays "Sign my letters".
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Writing: "If you can use fewer words, do so" (verified today). Airbnb category chips filling a field (repo COMPONENTS 1, observed).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: No change to data stored. VOICE multilingual rule still met in Settings and the store; D-056 language list unchanged.

screens.problem: Native script first, English second, one tap, Close in the corner. Nothing to fix.
screens.proposal: No change. Under Reduce Motion the sheet uses the 200 ms timing already specified.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Modality: "Always give people an obvious way to dismiss a modal view" (verified today); iOS Settings language list shows native and localized names (observed).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: D-056 seven languages, one per letter.

screens.screen: The book is open (finish step with the speech download ask)
screens.problem: The arrival line ("The book is open.") is right, then a card of three paragraphs explains a download: why the words are written on the phone, that it waits for Wi-Fi and resumes, and where to do it later. It is the most help-centre moment in the app, at the exact point the person should feel the door open.
screens.proposal: Keep the page drawing drawn on and the hero "The book is open." with its line "Say one thing about Asha today. That is a letter." Add the lamp wash (top anchor) so this screen matches the welcome: the two ends of first run share the light. Shrink the ask to one card with a title and one line: title "One download, 575 MB"; line "Spoken letters are written down on this phone. It waits for Wi-Fi."; two buttons inside the card, "Download on Wi-Fi" (secondary) and "Not now" (quiet). After Not now the card collapses to one line: "Your voice is kept either way." Delete "You can do this later in Settings, Recordings. Your voice is always kept." Primary stays "Write the first one", which lands on Tonight.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Onboarding: "Don't let large downloads hinder onboarding"; HIG Loading: "Improve installation and launch time by downloading large assets in the background" (verified today). Apple's own Siri and dictation language downloads are one row with a size and a Download control, no essay (memory, unverified).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: D-087: nothing downloads until the person taps; the explicit buttons keep that. The size shown must stay the real size for the phone.

screens.problem: The strongest screen in the app and already best-in-class in structure (time-of-day greeting, one prompt, twin Speak and Type, quiet Not much today). Two things hold it back: the subtitle "What do you want Asha to know about today?" is itself a prompt, so two questions stack above the prompt card; and the middle third is dead paper, with no light, no sense of evening, nothing from the website's atmosphere. Dark mode shows how good it could be.
screens.proposal: Delete the subtitle; the dateline, the greeting and the prompt card are the whole top. Add a LampWash anchored to the bottom behind Speak and Type, tone by the greeting key (amber for evening and night, dusk for lateNight, none for morning and midday), arriving once per cold launch and breathing only by opacity (tokens.motion.lamp on feat/mobile-calm-brand), off under Reduce Motion and Low Power. When a letter from about a month ago exists, show one quiet card between the prompt and the buttons: kicker "A month ago", the letter's first line in the reading face, tap opens it (the Day One resurfacing BENCHMARK already adopted); never a count, never a gap. Keep the waiting-letter card. Keep Speak and Type as identical twins at 64 pt. Deserves the light; no illustration.
screens.benchmark: Things 3 "This Evening" time framing (verified in repo BENCHMARK.md S8). Apple Journal: one reflection prompt instead of a blank page (verified in repo BENCHMARK.md S5). Day One "On This Day" resurfacing (verified in repo BENCHMARK.md S6). Website Evening scene: amber lamp behind one line (read on origin/main).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: No streaks, no days-since, no counts (content rules). The resurfaced card shows the person's own words untouched; the app writes nothing. Prompts stay the hand-written library; no daily-rhythm words in the app's own copy.

screens.screen: Tonight after Not much today (kept line with Undo)
screens.problem: A check, a line and an inline Undo in place of the link is exactly right. The line "Kept. Rest well." is wrong at 2 pm, which is when the screenshot was taken.
screens.proposal: Two strings keyed by the greeting: evening, night and lateNight say "Kept. Rest well."; earlier in the day say "Kept." Undo stays inline beside it. Haptic soft, as now.
screens.benchmark: Headspace's one-line warm confirmations without counters (verified in repo BENCHMARK.md S7). Apple HIG Feedback: confirmation matched to the significance of the action (verified today).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: D-084: a mark with no words; the app never writes a sentence for the person. No count, no streak.

screens.screen: Help us make it better (usage sharing ask)
screens.problem: Equal buttons and the calm timing are right. The sheet reads like a SaaS consent banner: a generic title, three paragraphs (what, that nothing is shared unless you say yes, where to change it) and a Close as a third way out.
screens.proposal: Title "Share usage reports?" One line: "Which screens open and when something breaks. Never your letters, recordings or names." Two equal outline buttons: "Don't share" and "Share". Delete "Nothing is shared unless you say yes. Saying no changes nothing else." Keep the Settings line only if counsel requires it for consent; otherwise drop it. Keep Close (closing without choosing asks at most once more).
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Privacy: purpose copy should be "a brief, complete sentence that's straightforward, specific, and easy to understand" (verified today). Apple's own analytics ask in Setup Assistant is one screen, two equal choices (memory, unverified).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: LEGAL-REQ-003: explicit opt-in on a consent sheet, declining changes nothing, withdrawal in Settings, Privacy takes effect at once. The proposal keeps the explicit equal choice; the Settings line is the only sentence counsel may insist on.

screens.problem: Full-screen, calm, one breathing glow, the audience line, Pause and Finish as equal twins, "Let it go" quiet. In light mode the disc reads a touch like an alarm red rather than the terracotta intended; dark mode is the reference.
screens.proposal: No structural change. Light mode: keep the disc at the recording token but lower the glow's peak opacity to the spec's 0.18 to 0.40 range so it reads as warmth, not warning. Leave the copy ("Listening." / "Say it however it comes." / "Still here. Take your time.") exactly as it is. This screen must stay quiet: no lamp wash, no illustration, no first-recording trust card.
screens.benchmark: Apple Watch Breathe and Calm pacing for the breathing glow (verified in repo MOTION.md M9, M10). Apple Voice Memos keeps one red control and no decoration (observed).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: The audience line "Only you, until you add it to the book." is the one privacy sentence on capture (VOICE table); keep it. MOTION principle 1: continuous motion only from a real signal.

screens.screen: Listen opened without a tap (ready state)
screens.problem: Right shape (StateScreen, one primary), reachable only by a stale route. The body explains twice: "Nothing is recording yet. Tap Start when you want to speak."
screens.proposal: Title "Ready when you are"; body "Nothing is recording yet."; button "Start". Keep Close top right.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Writing: "Avoid robotic error messages with no helpful information" and "If you can use fewer words, do so" (verified today).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: The microphone is not touched until Start (resilience start-intent); unchanged.

screens.problem: Calm card, Type first, Open Settings second: the right order. "We can't hear you yet" is a touch coy and uses the "we" voice Apple advises against in interface text.
screens.proposal: Title "The microphone is off"; body "Turn it on in Settings, or type this letter."; buttons "Type instead" (primary) and "Open Settings" (quiet); Close top right.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Writing: error messages should "avoid blame, and be clear about what someone can do to fix it"; "Avoid using we altogether" (verified today). HIG Privacy: ask in context, explain the benefit (verified today).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: Microphone purpose string stays the Info.plist sentence in permissions.en.ts; this card is in-app copy only.

screens.screen: Review while the words are being written down
screens.problem: The honest waiting state ("Writing down what you said.") with the recording kept first. On a phone the wait can be long for a first letter when the model is still downloading, and the screen offers no quiet way to keep going.
screens.proposal: Keep the InlineState with its breathing drawing and the line "Writing down what you said." Under it, two quiet options that already exist as strings: "Keep the recording" and "Type it instead". Never a spinner, never a percentage. When the speech model is not on the phone, the same card shows "Download on Wi-Fi" instead of waiting.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Loading: "Show something as soon as possible" and "Let people do other things in your app or game while they wait" (verified today).
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: ADR 0001 and TDD 03 FM-9: a recording kept before its words is never lost; words that arrive later arrive exactly as said (VOICE).

screens.screen: Review with words (small fixes, put back, exactly as said, change words)
screens.problem: The trust mechanics are best-in-class and nobody else has them: marks you can tap, "You said" and "Put it back", a reversible Undo, the two-view control. The screen is weighed down by reassurance in three layers: a permanent subtitle ("We only fixed what got in the way of your words. Nothing added."), the one-time note, and a footnote explaining private letters above the buttons.
screens.proposal: Delete the permanent subtitle; the title "Read it back" and the dateline are enough. Keep the one-time note (it is the disclosure) but let it collapse on "Got it" as now. Delete the footnote "Private letters stay with you. You can add them to the book later." and let "Keep private" carry that meaning. Keep the letter card, the "With small fixes | Exactly as said" control, the fixes list ("Took out a sound um,"), "Change words", "Add to Asha's book" primary and "Keep private" quiet. Motion: implement MOTION 5d exactly (inline card expands under the line; put back cross-fades with a 1.6 s accentSoft wash). No wash, no illustration: the words are the picture.
screens.benchmark: Apple HIG Writing: "Avoid using we altogether" and brevity (verified today). Things 3 in-place expansion (verified in repo MOTION.md M13). Day One keeps audio and transcript in one entry (verified in repo BENCHMARK.md S6); none of the named apps mark machine edits, which is this product's edge.
screens.legal_or_constitution_note: Constitution: every edit shown is one of the EditType kinds, verified by verifyEdits, reversible both ways; "Exactly as said" is only claimed when raw equals final (D-086). The first-time note is the in-app disclosure (in-app-disclosures.md 2); keep its sentence verbatim.

screens.problem: A typed letter has nothing to review (no fixes, no recording), yet it passes through a screen titled "Read it back" with the same explanatory footnote. One extra screen between typing and keeping.
screens.proposal: Skip Review for typed letters. On Write, replace the single "Save" with the destination pair that Review shows: primary "Add to Asha's book", quiet "Keep private" beneath it, both above the keyboard. Saving goes straight to the saved card (J07-04) and closes. The Plus gate, when it applies, opens from the same tap as today. If the pair cannot fit at AX sizes, stack them (ButtonRow already does).
screens.benchmark: Apple Notes and Bear: Done saves, there is no review step for typed text (memory, unverified). Apple HIG Modality: "keep modal tasks simple, short, and streamlined" (verified today).
